```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse  = TRUE,
  comment   = "#>",
  out.width = "100%",
  fig.width = 7,
  fig.height = 5,
  dpi       = 96,
  warning   = FALSE,
  message   = FALSE
)
```

In a complex-systems view of learning, a state is stable when students who
reach it tend to remain in it and students who leave it tend to return
(Saqr, Dever, et al. 2025; Saqr, López-Pernas & Tikka 2026). López-Pernas
and Saqr (2024) described student engagement in these terms, as the
momentum of achievement and the inertia of disengagement. Markov chain
theory measures stability from a transition network (Kemeny & Snell 1976).
For a first-order chain with transition matrix $P$ and stationary
distribution $\pi$:

- the *persistence* of state $i$ is $P_{ii}$, the probability of remaining
  in it at the next step;
- the *sojourn time* is $1 / (1 - P_{ii})$, the expected number of
  consecutive steps spent in it once entered;
- the *stationary probability* $\pi_i$ is the long-run share of steps spent
  in it, and the *return time* $1 / \pi_i$ is the expected number of steps
  between two visits;
- the *mean first passage time* $m_{ij}$ is the expected number of steps to
  reach state $j$ for the first time from state $i$.

In Nestimate (Saqr, López-Pernas & Misiejuk 2026), `passage_time()` returns
the matrix of mean first passage times and `markov_stability()` the
per-state measures. Both accept a network, a transition matrix, or a group
of networks.

## Data

`trajectories` records the engagement state of 138 students in each of the
15 successive courses of a program. The states are the three engagement
states of Saqr and López-Pernas (2021): `Active`, `Average` and
`Disengaged`. Saqr and López-Pernas (2021) and Saqr, López-Pernas, Jovanović
and Gašević (2023) followed such engagement trajectories across the courses
of a full program. The data have one row per student and one column per
course; a missing value occurs only as a run at the end of a row and marks
the point at which a student left the program.

## The transition network

`build_network()` estimates the probability of moving from each state to
each state between consecutive courses.

```{r network}
library(Nestimate)
net <- build_network(trajectories, method = "relative")
net
```

Each row of the matrix sums to 1. A student who is `Active` in one course
is `Active` in the next with probability 0.698, `Average` with probability
0.267 and `Disengaged` with probability 0.035. The measures below are
computed from this matrix, so they assume that the transition probabilities
are the same in every course and that the next state depends only on the
current one.

## Mean first passage times

```{r passage}
pt <- passage_time(net)
print(pt, digits = 2)
plot(pt)
```

Row $i$, column $j$ of the matrix is the expected number of courses for a
student in state $i$ to reach state $j$ for the first time; the diagonal is
the return time. A student in `Active` takes 3.6 courses on average to
reach `Average` and 10.4 courses to reach `Disengaged`. In the reverse
direction, a student in `Disengaged` takes 6.2 courses to reach `Active`
and 2.8 courses to reach `Average`. Decline from `Active` to `Disengaged`
is therefore slower than recovery in the opposite direction, and both pass
mostly through `Average`. The values are expectations under the fitted
chain; a value longer than the 15 courses of the program describes the
chain, not a time that was observed.

## Stability of the states

```{r stability}
ms <- markov_stability(net)
summary(ms)
plot(ms)
```

`persistence`, `stationary_prob`, `return_time` and `sojourn_time` are the
measures defined above. `avg_time_to_others` is the mean passage time from
the state to the other states, and `avg_time_from_others` the mean passage
time from the other states to it; a state with a short
`avg_time_from_others` is reached quickly from anywhere.

`Active` is the most persistent state: its persistence is 0.698 and its
sojourn time 3.31 courses. `Average` is the most accessible: it is reached
from the other states in 3.20 courses on average, and it has the largest
stationary probability, 0.443. `Disengaged` is the least persistent
(0.483, a sojourn of 1.93 courses) and the least accessible (9.16
courses), and it is the state students spend the least time in (0.185).

## Groups of students

A single chain for all students averages over students whose engagement
develops differently. Sequence clustering groups the students by the
similarity of their sequences (Saqr, López-Pernas, Helske, et al. 2024),
and a transition network can then be estimated for each group (López-Pernas,
Tikka & Saqr 2025). `build_clusters()` computes the Hamming distance
between sequences, the number of courses in which two students are in
different states (Hamming 1950), and partitions the students around
medoids (Kaufman & Rousseeuw 1990). Three clusters are used here as a
working choice.

```{r clusters}
clusters <- build_clusters(trajectories, k = 3, seed = 2026)
clusters
```

The three clusters have 47, 74 and 17 students. The average silhouette is
0.36 (Rousseeuw 1987), a moderate separation. `build_network()` on the
clustering estimates one transition network per cluster, and
`state_distribution()` shows the states that make up each cluster.

```{r cluster-networks}
cluster_networks <- build_network(clusters)
state_distribution(cluster_networks)
```

Cluster 1 is mostly `Active` (75% of its observed courses), cluster 2
mostly `Average` (60%), and cluster 3 mostly `Disengaged` (80%).

`passage_time()` and `markov_stability()` accept the group of networks and
compute the measures for each cluster. `summary()` returns one table with a
row for each cluster and state.

```{r cluster-passage, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 4}
cluster_pt <- passage_time(cluster_networks)
summary(cluster_pt)
plot(cluster_pt)
```

```{r cluster-stability}
cluster_ms <- markov_stability(cluster_networks)
summary(cluster_ms)
plot(cluster_ms)
```

In cluster 1, `Active` has persistence 0.805 and a sojourn time of 5.12
courses, and it is reached from the other states in 1.82 courses on
average. `Disengaged` is reached from the other states in 25.35 courses on
average, longer than the program: under this cluster's chain, students
rarely reach it. In cluster 2, `Average` is the most persistent state
(0.674, a sojourn of 3.06 courses) and the most accessible (1.89 courses),
and `Active` takes 8.94 courses to reach. In cluster 3, `Disengaged` has
persistence 0.889 and a sojourn time of 9.00 courses.

The estimates of cluster 3 rest on few observations. Its 17 students
contribute 2 transitions out of `Active` and 8 out of `Average`, so the
persistence of those two states (0.500 each) and the long passage times to
`Active` (39.50 courses from the other states) are not reliable. The
number of transitions out of each state can be checked with
`build_network(clusters, method = "frequency")` before the measures are
interpreted.
